headline: Tabled FY '27 budget transfer request, approved personnel actions via Consent Agenda, and discussed Waltham High School schedule and library strategic plan.
summary: The Committee heard updates on district safety training, a library strategic plan, and the Waltham High School scheduling process, but took no formal action on these topics. It approved the Consent Agenda covering new hires, retirements, resignations, and a donated vehicle for the CTE program, tabled the FY '27 Budget Transfer Request until the next meeting, and agreed to add a School Committee subcommittee proposal to the October 7, 2026 agenda.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including new hires, retirements, resignations, and a donated vehicle for the CTE program.
Agreed to add the School Committee subcommittee proposal to the October 7, 2026 meeting agenda.
Tabled the FY '27 Budget Transfer Request until the next meeting.

WALTHAM SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
 Waltham, Massachusetts 
 MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING  SEPTEMBER 16, 2026 
 RECESS 
 RECONVENE 
 PUBLIC INPUT 
 The regular meeting of the Waltham School Committee convened at 5:33pm. Present 
 were Ms. Wong-Bigelow, Mrs. AlJammal, Mrs. Coleman, and Mayor McCarthy.  Ms. 
 DeJoannis, Mr. Tarallo and Mr. Zanghi were not present.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 Mr. Zanghi arrived at 5:34pm. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to move to 
 Executive Session at 5:34pm to conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective 
 bargaining with the WSSA and / or to conduct negotiations with the WSSA; to 
 conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the WSAA and / 
 or to conduct negotiations with the WSAA; to conduct strategy sessions with respect 
 to collective bargaining with the Waltham School MIS Technicians and / or to conduct 
 negotiations with the Waltham School MIS Technicians; to conduct strategy sessions 
 with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham School Department Food 
 Service Workers; to conduct strategy sessions in preparation for negotiations with 
 nonunion personnel and/or to conduct negotiations with nonunion personnel  – 
 Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations; To conduct strategy sessions 
 with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers 
 Association and/or to conduct negotiations with the Waltham Building Maintenance 
 Workers Association, and in accordance with Mass. G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3), to 
 discuss strategy with respect to litigation if an open meeting may have a detrimental 
 effect on the litigating position of the  public body and the chair so declares - Waltham 
 School Secretaries Association and the Waltham Public Schools MUP-26-12223,  to 
 include Attorney Jonathan Atwater and Superintendent Dr. Mendonsa, and return to 
 the regular meeting at 7:00 pm.  All in favor. 
 The School Committee reconvened at 7:53pm.  Present were Mr. Tarallo, Mr. Zanghi, 
 Mrs. Coleman, Mrs. AlJammal, Ms. DeJoannis, Ms. Wong-Bigelow, and Mayor 
 McCarthy.  Mayor McCarthy presided. 
 The Committee recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 Mayor McCarthy announced the meeting was being recorded by WCAC. 
 Mr. Tarallo apologized for the delayed start but lengthy discussions about union 
 negotiations were taking place during the Committee’s Executive Session. 
 Waltham High School parent Nicole Piche-Nicholas again addressed the Committee 
 about the WHS schedule process and emphasized the importance of full 
 transparency, meaningful updates, an analysis of the pros and cons of each schedule 
 option, community forums, and feedback opportunities.  She reviewed the previously 
 communicated timeline and asked that information be shared about upcoming forums 
 and feedback opportunities.

 partner, The Stepping Stone Group, to build a WPS Safety and Risk Assessment
Minutes  __________ 
 CONSENT AGENDA 
 ____________________________  -3-                                      SEPTEMBER 16  , 2026 
 protocol, to revise the district’s manual, to compile a Behavioral and Safety Response 
 Playbook, to build a Readiness Workbook for each school, and to develop 
 standardized forms for response, documentation and review.  Additionally, the district 
 increased the number of internal CPI (Crisis Prevention Institute) instructors and, to 
 date, over 50 staff m  embers have been trained on this important de-escalation 
 process.  The goal is to triple this number by November.  Plympton Elementary will 
 be the primary focus of this work this year. 
 A request to receive progress updates from Plympton Elementary and about CPI 
 training of staff was made. 
 Dr. Shannon Conley advised that some of the district’s librarians were present to 
 share the Library Strategic Plan.  Director of Ed Tech and Library Sandy Malec 
 explained that the purpose of the library strategic plan is to align the programs and 
 curriculum across all school libraries for grades K-12. 
 Librarians Reba Tierney (WHS), Jen Ostayan (Northeast), Mary Kurspahic 
 (McDevitt), Liza Halley (Plympton), and Kristie Hanley (Whittemore) provided 
 background information, the why, the what, and the how of the strategic plan.  The 
 librarians emphasized the change in the district’s demographics along with declining 
 literacy rates as the driving forces behind this initiative.  The goals are: to continue to 
 instill and promote a love of reading, align with the curriculum and instruction, and 
 expand collaboration with partners to better support student learning.  Data was 
 shared about each school, including the number of books in circulation, the average 
 age of each school’s circulation, and the average number of available items per 
 student. 
 Ms. Tierney advised that Massachusetts passed the Freedom to Read law in August 
 of 2026 and it provides protections for librarians and booksellers and also requires 
 districts to have written policies for collection development and review. 
 Some of the members engaged the presenters in a conversation about classroom 
 libraries, available online reading apps for students, and community partnerships.

 Dr. Mendonsa suggested the Committee entertain adding two new subcommittees, 
 one for Finance and one for Curriculum and Instruction.  Currently, the policy 
 subcommittee is the only existing one.  The superintendent believes that much could 
 be accomplished between the three subcommittees and then information and 
 proposals could be shared with the whole committee at Regular Meetings. 
 Mayor McCarthy added that city-wide PTO meetings should be reinstated so 
 Committee members have a chance to hear from more people in the community 
 about school specific matters and larger issues.  A discussion with all of the 
 members and the superintendent followed and it was requested that a plan for each 
 of the subcommittees be brought to the next meeting. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to add this 
 matter to the October 7, 2026 agenda.  All in favor. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to table this matter 
 until the next meeting.  All in f  avor. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Ms. Wong-Bigelow, to pay the 
 bills on the warrant.  All in favor. 
 Dr. Mendonsa indicated that starting at the next meeting and running through 
 November, each of the school principals will be presenting their school improvement 
 plans to the Committee. 
 Ms. DeJoannis asked for a more detailed enrollment report for the middle schools 
 which includes specific class enrollment. 
 Additionally, Ms. DeJoannis requested a breakdown of course enrollment at Waltham 
 High.  She also requested information on the number of classes being co-taught and 
 the amount of professional development.  It was confirmed that this information will 
 be shared by Dr. Conard during his school improvement plan presentation. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs.Coleman, seconded by Mr. Tarallo, to adjourn the 
 Regular Meeting at 9:20pm. All in favor.
